newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin sees Russia WTO entry this year.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sees Russia WTO entry this year.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Sunday he expected Russia to join the World Trade Organisation this year.

"Russia must be in the WTO and eventually will get membership as it got membership of the Paris Club. I think it will happen this year and not in 1998," he told reporters after a morning meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.
He looked fit, there was colour in his cheeks and he spoke firmly and clearly, a few hours after skipping a Group of Seven concert because he was tired.

The G7 countries -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- have pledged to support Russian membership of the WTO and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.
But officials say Russia has not yet taken all the steps needed for membership and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Saturday that officials were targeting Russian WTO membership for 1998.

Indebted Russia won approval in principle during this G7 summit to join the Paris Club of creditor states as a creditor and Moscow officials said this was a big step towards Russia's financial integration with the rest of the world.
Yeltsin has been attending this year's annual G7 summit, dubbed "The Summit of the Eight".
